PullRequest.Title: sessions: Remove worktree cleanup from session context menu
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Removes Open Worktree Cleanup from each session's context menu while keeping it available from the Command Palette and Sessions More Actions menu. Updates the related accessibility help text to match.

Validation:
- Not run (per request).

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup registers the Open Worktree Cleanup action and its menu placements.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation constructs the Action2 descriptor and registers it; the diff removes one SessionItemContextMenu descriptor while retaining Command Palette and Sessions header registration. No asynchronous work or expensive boundary is on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One static action registration per workbench window; cost scales with the number of declared menu placements, which decreases from two explicit menu placements to one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, single registration during contribution loading; no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu metadata is held by the global registry for the window lifetime. The diff retains one fewer menu item; there are no cache misses or negative-cache states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk deletes only the SessionItemContextMenu object from the action descriptor.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact micro-cost of one menu descriptor is unmeasured, but the direction is strictly reduced allocation and registry work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Startup allocation and retained menu metadata decrease slightly, and no command handler work is executed during registration.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user opens a context menu for a session row.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI event builds a per-session context-key overlay, creates SessionItemContextMenu, evaluates visible actions, and renders the menu. The removed contribution is no longer evaluated or rendered; selecting other actions follows unchanged handlers.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One menu construction per context-menu opening; effective cardinality is the registered actions for that single menu, not the total session count. The action count decreases by one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-event handling for one opened context menu; repeated user openings are serialized by interaction and the previous menu disposable is replaced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static contributions come from MenuRegistry, while a fresh context overlay/menu instance is created for each opening. Removing the item avoids its condition evaluation on both cold and repeated openings; no cache is defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sessionsList.ts creates the same menu on demand, and the diff only removes one declarative contribution from that menu.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saved per-opening CPU/allocation is small and unmeasured, but there is no plausible increase in work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The changed path performs less menu evaluation and rendering work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A screen-reader user opens Sessions chat help or worktree-cleanup editor help.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible help creation synchronously localizes fixed strings, stores them in a short array, and joins them when content is requested. The diff shortens two fixed strings and adds no service call or deferred work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed-size string construction per help-provider invocation; content size does not scale with sessions or worktrees.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on-demand provider construction; no parallelism, limiter, queue, or backpressure is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is involved. Localization lookup behavior is unchanged, using the same keys, and the resulting strings are slightly shorter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both accessibility hunks alter only literal text passed to existing localize calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: String allocation savings are negligible and unmeasured, but the change cannot create scaling work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. CPU and allocation are unchanged in cardinality and marginally reduced in bytes.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user invokes Open Worktree Cleanup from the remaining Command Palette, Sessions More Actions menu, or storage suggestion.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unchanged action suppresses the suggestion and opens SessionWorktreeCleanupEditor. The editor then awaits getWorktrees before rendering rows; a cold measurement is therefore on the editor-content critical path, while warm measurements reuse cached results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure session worktree disk usage via ISessionsManagementService.getSessionWorktreeDiskUsage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one disk-usage call per worktree-owning session on a cold measurement, with two calls active concurrently; warm and coalesced requests reuse one-hour cached/shared results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor command and bounded/cached measurement ran after selecting Open Worktree Cleanup from any prior surface; the diff removes the session-row context-menu surface and leaves all execution code unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold scan must complete before the cleanup editor renders its worktree rows; it is not performed merely by opening a session context menu or accessibility help.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold disk-usage measurement scales with sessions that own worktrees, grouped per session; each session measurement accounts for its distinct worktrees. Menu removal does not increase this effective cardinality and removes one former invocation surface.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disk usage calls are bounded by Limiter(2), concurrent measurements for the same session signature are coalesced, and each call has a 10-second timeout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Measured worktrees are cached for one hour when the session signature is unchanged; concurrent requests share one measurement. Session changes invalidate timestamps/signatures as before. The diff does not change cache keys, success/failure behavior, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action handler and cleanup service are unchanged, and the deleted descriptor was only an additional menu entry pointing to the same command.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual scan duration depends on the number and location of worktrees, but neither call count, concurrency, cache behavior, nor critical-path placement is increased by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Existing filesystem work remains bounded and cached behind explicit command invocation, while the diff only removes one way to invoke it.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced startup registration, per-session menu construction, accessibility help generation, and the remaining cleanup-editor filesystem path. The PR removes one static/per-open menu item and shortens fixed help text; it adds no work, retention, fan-out, boundary call, concurrency, or critical-path latency. No performance findings were submitted.
